bib.title: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories. Shuai Shao, Kangning Zhang, Qingyao Li, et al. (SJTU, Xiaohongshu). arXiv:2608.02276v1, 3 Aug 2026, preprint. Code: github.com/DeepExperience/Harness-R1.
COVERAGE: 22 of 22 pages read; 74,912 of 74,912 chars, including appendices A-H. The reference list (about chars 25000-48000) was only skimmed. Extraction was clean, except that figure-internal text (Fig 1, Fig 3, Fig 4) came out as number lists. I also read notes/02-harness-anatomy.md.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: A separate 9B "harness engineer" trained with SFT then online GRPO raises a frozen Qwen3.5-9B target's average success on three benchmarks from 44.3% to 53.6%.
  number: +9.3 pp
  setup: WebShop (500 tasks), ALFWorld (500), DBBench (300). Avg is the equal-weight mean of WebShop Succ., ALFWorld All and DBBench Succ. Target temperature 0, thinking disabled. Single run, no confidence intervals in Table 1. Reward is computed on the same tasks used to mine the failures.
  quote: "Harness-R1 raises vanilla Qwen3.5-9B success from 44.3% to 53.6% (+9.3 percentage points)."
  where: abstract, p1; Table 1, p7
- claim: Prompting frontier models as harness editors is unreliable and sometimes harmful. The best, GLM-5.2, reaches 48.8% average, below Harness-R1. A supervised-only engineer reaches 46.4%.
  number: GLM-5.2 48.8%; GPT-5.5 47.9%; Qwen3.5-397B 45.8%; supervised-only 46.4%; Self-Refine 41.8% (-2.5 vs 44.3)
  setup: Same target and task set as above. Frontier editors see the failure packet once and never rerun the target. Reflection (55.8%) uses a two-episode success@2 protocol and is not comparable. ReAct 47.5%.
  quote: "Among frontier engineers, the strongest is GLM-5.2 at a 48.8% average, below Harness-R1 at 53.6%."
  where: Sec 4.2, p7; Table 1
- claim: The harness gain persists after the target is fine-tuned. An engineer retrained for the SFT'd target adds 5.0 pp.
  number: 59.2% to 64.2%
  setup: Qwen3.5-9B SFT'd on 2,515 successful trajectories (901 WebShop, 774 ALFWorld, 840 DBBench). The engineer was retrained for this target. One adaptation step; multi-round co-evolution is not tested. The ALFWorld gain is large (71.2 to 84.0), while WebShop Score and DBBench move little (DBBench 63.7 to 65.7).
  quote: "a target-specific Harness-R1 engineer trained for this stronger actor raises it further to 64.2%, an additional 5.0 points."
  where: Sec 4.2, p7
- claim: Lifecycle-position ablation. Removing pre-action mediation (guardrail on the proposed action) or post-feedback recovery costs the most. Removing episode-start or pre-decision edits costs under 1 pp. The ranking is environment-dependent and the authors say it is not additive.
  number: full 53.1%; no intervention 44.2%; w/o pre-action 49.2% (-3.9); w/o post-feedback 49.8% (-3.3); w/o episode init 52.2% (-0.9); w/o pre-decision 52.5% (-0.6)
  setup: Fixed generated patches on vanilla Qwen3.5-9B. Three reruns per benchmark. This is a removal ablation. Per benchmark (Table G.1): WebShop pre-action 41.6 to 31.5 (the WebShop patches contain only pre-action edits); ALFWorld post-feedback 52.1 to 41.9. DBBench is flat.
  quote: "Removing pre-action mediation or post-feedback recovery reduces success by 3.9 and 3.3 points, whereas removing episode-start or pre-decision changes costs 0.9 and 0.6 points."
  where: Sec 4.5, p9; Table G.1, p19
- claim: The single trained editing policy transfers to 20 unseen target models of different families and sizes, with a patch generated per target from that target's own failures.
  number: +7.06 pp mean over 20 unseen targets; 56 of 63 target-benchmark cells improve, 4 unchanged, 3 small regressions (at most 2.0 pp)
  setup: Llama 3.x, Gemma 3/4, Qwen2.5/3/3.5/3.6 from 1B to 72B. Single run each. Large gains on small models (Qwen3-4B +12.3, Gemma-3-4B +12.0), small gains on the strongest (Qwen2.5-72B +1.0, Qwen3.5-27B +3.6). 1B models gain about nothing (Llama-3.2-1B +2.2, Gemma-3-1B +1.2).
  quote: "Across twenty unseen target configurations, the benchmark-averaged gain is 7.06 percentage points, and every target-level average is positive."
  where: Sec 4.3, p8; Table E.1, p19
- claim: Patches written from only 10 failures generalize to held-out tasks for Harness-R1. The same protocol with frontier editors gives negative or zero mean change.
  number: Harness-R1 +8.9±1.5; Qwen3.5-397B -4.3±2.5; DeepSeek-V4-Pro -0.4±3.6
  setup: Frozen Qwen3.5-9B. One patch per benchmark per seed, 3 seeds (sample std), 1,270 pooled held-out tasks. Valid patches: Harness-R1 9/9, Qwen3.5-397B 8/9, DeepSeek-V4-Pro 6/9.
  quote: "Harness-R1 improves pooled held-out success by 8.9±1.5 percentage points and is positive for all three seeds."
  where: Sec 4.4, p8; Table F.1, p19
- claim: A plausible-looking patch from a strong model can make the agent worse. Gemini-3.5-Flash's broad force-action rules cut ALFWorld success.
  number: 208/500 (41.6%) to 177/500 (35.4%); of 39 valid patches, 21 reduce, 12 improve, 6 unchanged; worst batch 7/10 to 0/10
  setup: ALFWorld, frozen Qwen3.5-9B, patches that edit all four hooks, including on_before_action rules that force actions from a stage estimate.
  quote: "Its patches reduce success from 208/500 (41.6%) to 177/500 (35.4%), a drop of 6.2 percentage points."
  where: App H.3, p21
- claim: A narrow guard can give most of a gain. A WebShop pre-action hook blocks "Buy Now" when the price exceeds the budget or a required option is unselected.
  number: 2/10 to 5/10 full successes; mean reward 0.682 to 0.768
  setup: One 10-task batch (case study, chosen by the authors, not an aggregate). The authors say these cases are illustrative.
  quote: "the same guard raises full successes from 2 to 5 and mean WebShop reward from 0.682 to 0.768, while preserving both tasks that were already fully successful."
  where: App H.1, p20
- claim: Reward design. The engineer's reward is the full-batch mean reward change when the same frozen target reruns the tasks with the patch installed, including tasks that already succeeded. Invalid, no-op or incomplete patches get 0. Regressions give negative reward.
  number: K=8 candidates per packet; reward = (1/n) sum (R_patched - R_base)
  setup: Group-normalized GRPO, no KL, no format bonus. SFT data is 877 teacher (GPT-5.5) examples filtered for non-negative reward change (381 WebShop, 248 ALFWorld, 248 DBBench). The abstract's "roughly 1,000" and the appendix's 877 differ. About 1,500 failure packets for RL. 8x H800.
  quote: "r(B, P) = ∆B(P), if valid and complete, 0, otherwise."
  where: Eq. 1, p4-5; App B, p15-16
- claim: Four lifecycle hook positions form the editable surface of an existing runtime. The hooks only touch inputs and outputs around the frozen policy, and the host runtime interprets their structured effects.
  number: none
  setup: Hooks are on_init, make_pre_hint, on_before_action and on_post_step. Table C.1 covers returns (inject hint, block_and_prompt, rewrite_action, force_action). DBBench v1 allows only soft guidance and blocking.
  quote: "(i) episode initialization sets up the starting context and episode state; (ii) pre-decision augments the context with retrieved guidance and interface constraints before the agent decides; (iii) pre-action is a runtime guardrail that may canonicalize, rewrite, or veto the proposed action before it reaches the environment; and (iv) post-feedback inspects the returned observation and triggers recovery when the trajectory stalls."
  where: Sec 3.1, p4; App C, p17
- claim: Fixed hand-designed strategies are not universally helpful. Self-Refine lowers reward on all three benchmarks, and ReAct gives a limited gain.
  number: Self-Refine -3.3 average reward change in Fig 1 (text says 2.6 for reward, 2.5 for success); ReAct +3.2 success
  setup: Same Qwen3.5-9B target. The figure and prose disagree slightly on the Self-Refine figure.
  quote: "ReAct improves the average by 3.2 points, whereas Self-Refine reduces it by 2.5 points."
  where: Sec 4.2, p7; Fig 1, p2

LIMITS
- The authors concede: only one vanilla-to-fine-tuned adaptation is tested, with no multi-round co-evolution. The reward is same-batch and transductive, so it is tied to the tasks used to mine failures. There is no held-out or efficiency term in the reward. Patches are not guaranteed regression-free (ALFWorld case: 6 rescued, 1 regressed; stage tracking can loop).
- Only three environments (WebShop, ALFWorld, DBBench), all short-horizon and text-based. No coding or terminal benchmarks. This differs from Terminal-Bench-style settings, so it does not carry over to coding harnesses.
- No confidence intervals on Table 1 or the transfer table. The ablation has 3 reruns and the held-out test has 3 seeds. Targets run at temperature 0.
- Hooks are a hand-designed interface per benchmark, with benchmark-specific runtime context (predicates and state) exposed to the engineer. Gains depend on that context. Part of the gain may come from environment-specific guards.
- Patch runtime cost is not measured. Non-additivity of hook effects is stated.
- Frontier editors were compared with one prompt and no reruns. This tests "one-shot, no feedback", not the best achievable prompted editing. The model names are 2026 releases (GPT-5.5, GLM-5.2, etc.) and will date.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Shao et al. 2024 (GRPO)
- Madaan et al. 2023 (Self-Refine); Shinn et al. 2023 (Reflection); Yao et al. 2023b (ReAct)
- Harness-evolution systems: Lee et al. 2026 (Meta-Harness), Lin et al. 2026 (Agentic Harness Engineering), Lou et al. 2026 (AutoHarness), Xu et al. 2026 (Life-Harness), Chen et al. 2026b (HarnessX), Chen et al. 2026a (diagnosing and repairing harness flaws), Karten et al. 2026 (Continual Harness)
- Prompt optimization: APE (Zhou 2023), OPRO (Yang 2024), ProTeGi (Pryzant 2023), TextGrad (Yuksekgonul 2025), EvoPrompt, Promptbreeder (Fernando 2023), GEPA (Agrawal 2026), DSPy (Khattab 2023), MIPRO (Opsahl-Ong 2024)
- Benchmarks: WebShop (Yao 2023a), ALFWorld (Shridhar 2021), DBBench in AgentBench (Liu 2025)

CODE
- Engineer output contract (App A.1, p13):
  ADD_CODE_HOOK ::= { "type": "add_code_hook", "hook": "on_init" | "make_pre_hint" | "on_before_action" | "on_post_step", "code": "<PYTHON SOURCE DEFINING hook(ctx, nb)>" }
- Hook return contracts (App A.1, p13): "on_init -> skills/tool_hint or None; make_pre_hint -> message or None; on_before_action -> block_and_prompt, rewrite_action, or force_action; on_post_step -> inject_hint or, where supported, force_action"
- Fig 2 pseudo-hooks (p3): on_init returns skills and tool_hint; make_pre_hint says "Before buying, verify the price"; on_before_action returns "Do not buy this item" if product_price_over_budget; on_post_step flags repeated or looping.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p2): Matched-baseline reward change for Self-Refine (-3.3), Kimi K2.6 (+0.1), DeepSeek V4 (+1.0), Qwen 397B (+1.1), GLM 5.2 (+3.7) and Harness-R1 (+7.0). It shows that prompted editors are unreliable.
- Fig 2 (p3): Loop diagram. Failure trajectories lead to the 9B engineer, which writes a patch with four lifecycle hooks (Episode-Init, Pre-Decision, Pre-Action, Post-Feedback) around a frozen LLM. Task success feeds the GRPO update of the engineer only. This is the best single picture of the four hook positions, and it could map onto the note's Feedback and Tools subsystems.
- Fig 3 (p8): 21-target by 3-benchmark heatmap of gains.
- Fig 4 (p8): (a) held-out generalization bars; (b) lifecycle ablation.
- Not run through figures.py; captions taken from the extraction.

NOTE-RELEVANCE (for the caller; facts only)
- Note 02 already cites AHE (Lin et al. 2026) and LIFE-Harness (Xu et al. 2026). This paper's ablation is a removal ablation over lifecycle hook positions. It is a third data point for "interface and guard layers matter". Its pre-action and post-feedback positions correspond to the note's hooks/middleware (component 8) and the Feedback subsystem.
- It is not about the anatomy per se. It treats the harness as an editable surface and trains the editor. A different reading is that the 4 hook points are a minimal runtime-surface taxonomy (init, pre-decision, pre-action, post-feedback).

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found in the PDF. The Fig 1 vs prose discrepancy for Self-Refine (-3.3 vs "2.6" and "2.5") is in the source. The SFT example count is "roughly 1,000" in the body and 877 in App B.1. The note's mention "LIFE-Harness ... (Xu et al., 2026-10)" is not checked against this paper, which cites only "Xu et al., 2026".
